title: Ringo Starr marries Barbara Bach | 1981
content:
Ringo Starr married Barbara Bach on 27 April 1981.

The wedding took place at Marylebone Register Office, where Paul McCartney had married Linda Eastman on 12 March 1969. On 9 October 2011 McCartney married Nancy Shevell at the same venue.

Bach’s dress was designed by Emmanuel’s in London. At the time the firm was also designing the dress for Lady Diana’s wedding to Prince Charles in July 1981.

Starr and Bach were married by registrar Joseph Jevans, who had officiated at Paul and Linda’s 1969 wedding. The McCartneys were among the guests, as were George and Olivia Harrison. Other guests included Neil Aspinall, Derek Taylor, Harry Nilsson, and Starr’s mother and stepfather Elsie and Harry.

During the reception, held at Mayfair nightclub Rags, Starr shared a stage with McCartney and Harrison for the first time since 1969, performing several rock ‘n’ roll hits and ending the impromptu set with ‘I Saw Her Standing There’ and ‘Twist And Shout’. Harrison played guitar, McCartney and Nilsson took turns at the piano, and Starr and Ray Cooper played teaspoon percussion.

Embed from Getty Images

Starr met Bach, a model and actor who appeared in The Spy Who Loved Me, on the set of Caveman in Mexico in 1980. At the time Starr was with Nancy Lee Andrews, but by the end of the shoot in March 1980 he and Bach were a couple.

Within a year of the wedding, however, there were reports of violent arguments in which bottles and punches were thrown. She too became a heavy drinker. “Barbara fell into the trap because of me,” Starr said in 1989. “She was an actress who used to go to bed at ten at night and get up at eight in the morning. Till we met. Then her career went the same way as mine. I did two records, a few shows. But working two days a year is not having a career.” She did attempt to get their excesses under control, though to little success. “Every couple of months she’d try and straighten us out,” Starr recalled, “but then we’d fall right back into the trap.”

On Friday 7 October 1988 Starr and Bach finally hit rock bottom. Their binges and blackouts had become public knowledge, as had their physical violence towards one another, but that afternoon he awoke to a scene of utter destruction.

“I came to one Friday afternoon and was told by the staff that I had trashed the house so badly they thought there had been burglars, and I’d trashed Barbara so badly they thought she was dead,” he said. Neither could remember the fight due to their excessive drinking, but it was clear that something had to end.

Against the odds, the brutal incident did not spell the end of their marriage. Instead they both pledged to get help, a resolution which strengthened the bond between them.

This was just the end of the line for me. I’d had enough and I’d caused a lot of damage. I had come out of a huge blackout. I said, ‘You’ve got to get us into one of the places. We need help.’ And she did.
Ringo Starr

They were admitted into the Sierra Tucson treatment centre in Arizona, and remained in rehab for six weeks, at a reported cost of $35,000 each. Starr overcame his initial resistance and embraced the treatments: “Eight days in, I decided, ‘I’m here to get help because I know I’m sick.’ And I just did whatever they asked me and, thank God, it pulled me through. I can never thank that clinic enough.”
